findings.title: Concept write has no create-only or merge rule, so a run can overwrite the User-Provided Concept
findings.description: Flow step 5 ("Draft. Emit the planning artifacts," L143-144) and the concept output (L148-151) write `000-concept.{project}.md` with no existence check. `CLAUDE.md` L75-76 says "## User-Provided Concept" must be preserved exactly and never modified or removed. L150 restates this as "never rewritten," but nothing in the flow enforces it. The "refresh" path (L131) re-runs the same skill against the same target, and the doc gives no rule for that case. Analysis outputs get a new index per run (L251-252), so they cannot collide, but the concept path is fixed, so the overwrite risk is real. Before slice design, the concept must be create-only. If it exists, the skill should stop and show the diff. Any merge must leave the sacred section byte-identical. Nothing should be written until the draft is complete (see the partial-write issue in the failure-modes finding).

findings.title: Staleness check fires on every run after the graph is committed, and "commit distance" is undefined in common cases
findings.description: `meta.json.gitCommitHash` is HEAD at analysis time (L86). A commit cannot contain its own hash. Once the regenerated graph is committed (L186-187 says it is tracked), the recorded hash is always at least one commit behind HEAD. The warning therefore fires on the first squadron run after every graph commit. The signal is systematically false, and the PM will learn to ignore it. "Commit distance" (L131) is undefined when the hash is unreachable (rebase, squash, shallow CI clone, graph copied from another branch), and no fallback is given. `analyzedFiles` (L86) would give a meaningful signal (did any analyzed file change?) and is unused. `config.json`'s `autoUpdate` (L87) is read, but its effect on staleness is not stated. If the plugin refreshes the graph on its own, squadron's drift check reasons about a graph it did not produce. The provenance the warning "must appear in" (L134-135, L334-335) is not a field in either output schema (L148-156, L216-226).

findings.title: Tracking the regenerated graph in git is unexamined: churn, merge conflicts, and committed summaries
findings.description: The graph is a per-file LLM summary store (L94-97) regenerated by a nondeterministic process. Each regeneration rewrites much of it, so every regen produces a large diff, and concurrent branches conflict on it. The doc calls it "durable project knowledge" without addressing either problem. Summaries of `config:` nodes are committed too, and nothing reviews them for secrets or sensitive values. The file set is also incomplete. `intermediate/scan-result.json` (L88) appears in neither the ignore list (L180-184) nor the tracked list (L186-187), so it will show as untracked after the first run unless upstream ignores it itself. The doc does not say which. The design should state a track/ignore decision per file with a reason, measure graph size and diff churn on squadron's own repo, and say how conflicts are resolved (regenerate rather than merge, or do not track).

findings.title: The "plugin installed" precondition blocks reading a committed graph
findings.description: Step 1 requires verifying that the plugin is installed before reading. But the graph is committed (L186-187) as project knowledge. A teammate who clones the repo gets the graph without the plugin and is blocked from reading it. The plugin is needed only to regenerate. The doc also never says how the skill detects the plugin. L296 says the skill "detects absence and instructs," with no mechanism. The framing is inconsistent: L56-58 says the graph is "an input, not a dependency," yet L309-310 lists the plugin under Dependencies. Fix: block only on a missing graph, require the plugin only for regeneration, and name the detection method.

findings.title: Failure modes are specified only for "graph missing" and "graph stale"
findings.description: Not specified: (a) a malformed or truncated `knowledge-graph.json` from a crashed or interrupted plugin run; (b) schema drift, since there is no version check on read despite L40-41 noting active upstream development; (c) an empty or missing `tour[]`, since tour is Phase 6 of `/understand` (L101-103), which can be skipped or fail, while the design treats it as a key input (L104-105); (d) zero file-level nodes or layers; (e) an unreachable `gitCommitHash` (see the staleness finding); (f) a failed `.gitignore` write; (g) an interview aborted midway. Step 2 writes `.gitignore` (L136-137) before the interview, so an aborted run leaves a modified tracked file and no outputs. `CLAUDE.md` L8 forbids silent fallback values and requires explicit failure. Each case needs a named stop message, a defined partial-state rule, or an explicit flagged unknown in the document.

findings.title: The design hard-codes upstream internals with no version pin, and the gitignore entry outlives the plugin
findings.description: The design encodes upstream's Phase numbers (0, 6, 7), the `.trash-<epoch>/` naming, the 7-day purge, and issue #301's rationale as stable contract. It names only v2.8.1 (L71), with no pin, compatibility range, or re-validation trigger. The graph-shape section (L92) is attributed to "the plugin's own reference" with no link or version. If upstream renames `.trash-` or changes node types, the `.gitignore` entry silently stops matching and reads fail with no detection. The reverse also holds. After uninstall, nothing purges trash, and the gitignore entry hides it from `git status`, so trash accumulates unseen. Fix: record the validated plugin version in provenance, validate expected keys on read and fail explicitly on mismatch, and state what squadron does on uninstall.

findings.title: The read discipline cannot be executed with the tools a markdown skill has
findings.description: L107 says "Grep for the needed section before reading." JSON has no sections. Selecting file-level nodes by `type` requires parsing `nodes[]`, which Grep and Read cannot do. On a minified file, Grep returns entire lines. The installer copies markdown only (L295-296), so no helper script ships with the skill, and the doc names no parser. jq is not a declared dependency. There is also no budget. L138-139 extracts a `summary` for every file-level node, and the design never estimates that cost on squadron's own repo. The prior art the doc calls "materially lighter on token use" (L263-267) uses a Python probe script, so the chosen path is the heavier one and the comparison is unquantified. `CLAUDE.md` L40-43 requires a parser test fixture that uses the real format. The plan has none.

findings.title: Edges are never read, but two outputs depend on them
findings.description: Step 3 (L138-139) extracts project, layers, tour, and file-level nodes. Edges are not in the set. The analysis output needs "dependency observations" (L152-153), and Initial Technical Direction needs "languages, frameworks, dependencies" (L168). Dependencies come from `imports` and `depends_on` edges (L96-97), which the flow never reads. The node shape (L94) has no languages or frameworks field; it has `tags[]` and `languageNotes?`, so the source for those is undefined. "Entry points" (L153) has no stated derivation either. `endpoint` is listed as a node type (L108), but the doc does not say entry points are endpoints.

findings.title: Translation examples contradict the rules they illustrate, and one is a hallucination trap
findings.description: (a) L231 maps "Initiative 140 status draft" to "foundational work, in progress." `draft` is not in the initiative plan's vocabulary (`project-documents/user/project-guides/001-initiative-plan.squadron.md` uses `in_progress`, `not_started`, and `deferred`, e.g., lines 21-25, where 140 is `in_progress`). It is also rejected by the frontmatter enum the doc cites (L260-261). Mapping it to "in progress" breaks "Status is honest" (L236-237), since not-started work must read as planned. "Foundational" is an invented classification. (b) L233 maps "Weighted review convergence with decay-based finding dismissal" to "automated review that converges without human babysitting." "Without human babysitting" is not in the source (initiative 180, plan line 23), and L234-235 forbids exactly this kind of addition. `CLAUDE.md` L45-59 describes the failure: a concrete example placed near a retrieval instruction is reproduced when the source is empty. Replace these with examples that flag an unsupported outcome for PM input, and give the status mapping as an explicit table.

findings.title: Capability 2 has no flow, no input gate, and an undefined path for the common case
findings.description: The Flow section (L125-144) covers only Capability 1. Capability 2 has inputs (L194-200) and a field table (L216-226) but no steps. The doc calls the concept-absent case "the tested path" (L199-200). In that case three of nine fields have no source: Problem (sourced to the concept, L219), Audience (L220), and Approach (L221). L197-199 says purpose comes from "the initiative plan plus interview," but no interview is defined for Capability 2. The question table (L163-169) belongs to Capability 1. The initiative plan is "Required" (L196), with no behavior specified if it is absent or if several plan files exist. There is no minimum-answers threshold. If the PM declines everything, the document ships with empty fields. "Degrades gracefully" is a silent fallback in `CLAUDE.md`'s sense (L8) unless each degraded field becomes an explicit flagged unknown. The doc requires that for Capability 1 only (L171-172).

findings.title: The client-facing document has no review or sensitivity gate
findings.description: The output is for clients (L22-23) and is written directly to `project-documents/user/analysis/`. No PM review step is defined. Only initiative candidates need confirmation (L154-156). Its inputs include interview answers, the concept, and initiative-plan "notes" (Risks, L226). Any of these can be internal-only: commercial terms, staffing, internal politics, or a deprecated approach. The doc has no tagging, exclusion, or redaction rule. It names overstated status as "a liability" (L236-237), but the larger liability is an unreviewed, external-facing file. Fix: mark the draft as not reviewed for external use until the PM approves it, and define how internal-only content is excluded.

findings.title: Index allocation states three different rules, and the overflow band is already occupied
findings.description: L254-255 says overflow goes "into 950+." L256-257 says "remaining slots in the 900 band." The resolved decision at L332-333 says outputs go "in the 940-949 reserved range." Each run is a new sample (L251-252), so every `/sq:overview` or `/sq:analysis understand` run consumes a slot. Seven remain (943–949), and no supersession rule exists even though `deprecated` is in the status enum (L260-261). The 900 band is not empty in this repo. Initiative 900 is in the plan (`project-documents/user/project-guides/001-initiative-plan.squadron.md:35`), and task indices 901–915 are in use (e.g., `tasks/910-…` and `tasks/915-…`). The doc does not say whether indices are unique per kind or globally. L249-250 describes 940–949 as "codebase analysis, research, investigation," which a client overview does not match. L256-258 calls the problem "not a blocker," but this design creates the pressure. The naming convention the doc defers to is not in this worktree, so the reservation itself is unverified.

findings.title: Audience handling is decided three different ways
findings.description: L64-66 says audience separation "is a document boundary, not a tone setting." L238-239 says audience variants "differ in emphasis" and that "emphasis is a generation parameter." L328-331 resolves "one neutral document" and adds an emphasis parameter only "if real use demonstrates the need." The translation rules rely on a parameter the resolved decisions defer. Remove the parameter from L238-239, or change L328-331. If emphasis is selection rather than tone, reconcile it with L64-66.

findings.title: Initiative-plan candidate generation, the hardest step, is one clause with no storage, numbering, or lifecycle
findings.description: "Derived from layer boundaries and complexity clustering" (L154-155) names no clustering method. The value type of `complexity` is not given anywhere (L94). The doc names no output format or path, no index assignment for new initiatives (the plan is a single numbered registry file, `001-initiative-plan`), and no behavior for a declined candidate. Is it discarded, kept in chat, or written as a draft? Candidates in the planning tree would be visible to `cf` and downstream phases, which L44-45 says must consume outputs unchanged. The Open Questions (L337-342) omit this entirely. This is the most cuttable part of Capability 1. L156's own rule ("an unreviewed generated one is worse than none") supports deferring it to a follow-up slice.

findings.title: The codebase-comprehension analysis document is descriptive, duplicates the graph, and contradicts the "no overlap" claim
findings.description: L119 calls squadron's capability prescriptive, with "no functional overlap" with onboard and explain (L114-121). But the analysis output (L152-153) is "layers, complexity hotspots, entry points, dependency observations." That is the descriptive content onboard renders (L114-116). It is also a snapshot of graph data that goes stale when written, with no regeneration path or staleness marker of its own. It consumes a 940–949 slot per run (L251-252). Proportionality: the motivating gap (L32-34) is the missing concept, and the doc's own rule (L51-52) is that derived artifacts restate and do not add claims. Cut this output. If a structural summary is wanted, render it on demand and do not commit it.

findings.title: The tour is an onboarding reading order, presented as a Solution Approach signal
findings.description: L99 defines the tour as "5–15 pedagogical steps," built to teach a newcomer. L104-105 calls its ordering "expert judgment about which components matter" and "a strong signal for a concept's Solution Approach section." Reading order and solution structure are different things. The tour is also LLM-generated by the tour-builder agent (L101-103), so it is not "expert judgment" in the sense L46-48 uses, and it is not PM intent. Using it as a Solution Approach input launders an onboarding sequence into a concept document. Use layers as the primary structural source, treat the tour as an unverified cross-check, and label its provenance.

findings.title: Dependencies section omits real dependencies and does not say whether `/sq:overview` needs CLI registration
findings.description: The section lists [100], [340], and the plugin. Omitted: `cf`. The frontmatter gate runs `cf validate frontmatter` on every commit (`src/squadron/events/builtin/frontmatter_gate.py:44`), and the no-gate-change claim (L246-247) depends on it. Also omitted: the concept guide and naming convention, whose section names the interview and field tables cite (L163-169, L218-221); the initiative plan's inline `Status:` format (`001-initiative-plan` lines 21-25), which Capability 2 must parse; and the upstream JSON schema. [100] is listed as "CLI command registration for any command surface" (L307), yet Delivery (L281-289) never says whether `/sq:overview` needs registration. Capability 2 also depends on Capability 1's concept (L196-197). The claim that the two share "nothing else" (L16-17) is therefore inaccurate, and the handoff should be stated.

findings.title: Current-state claims mostly check out; several load-bearing references are not verifiable from this worktree
findings.description: Verified against the repo: `commands/sq/analysis.md:7` routes only `tech-debt-audit`. `.gitignore` has no `understand` or `trash` entry. `commands/sq/` has no `overview` command, so `/sq:overview` does not collide, and `summary.md` exists (L288-289). Only 940–942 are consumed in the 94x analysis range. `src/squadron/data/skills.toml` names the pack without listing its files, so "no manifest change" (L278-279) holds. Not verifiable here: `file-naming-conventions.md`, the concept guide, and `guide.ai-project.process`. `CLAUDE.md` L62-66 references them, but `project-documents/ai-project-guide/` is absent from this worktree. The 940–949 reservation (L249) and the frontmatter enum (L260-261) are therefore unconfirmed. The enum is enforced by `cf validate frontmatter`. The plugin version (L71) is dated 20260818 and is unverified against current upstream.

findings.title: The placement rule is applied asymmetrically
findings.description: Capability (b) stays out of the analysis dispatcher because it "audits nothing" (L282-283). Capability (a) writes a concept and initiative candidates, which are planning artifacts, yet it is placed in the analysis dispatcher (L273-274). Either the real criterion is "writes docType analysis" (then say so), or (a) belongs alongside (b). Stakes are low, but the stated rule does not decide the case it is applied to.

findings.title: The retained prior-art prompt has no decision rule for choosing between two comprehension paths
findings.description: The doc keeps `analyze-codebase-prompt.md` as a "low-cost alternative path" (L266-267). It gives no criteria for when a PM should pick it over `understand`, no owner, and an open question about reusing it (L341-342). That is two comprehension paths with one unselected. Define the selection rule, or remove the alternative from this design. `CLAUDE.md` L7 asks for resistance to added complexity.

findings.title: Interview question list in Flow does not match the scope table
findings.description: Step 4 (L140-142) asks about "business context" and "known constraints." The scope table (L163-169) has no such sections. It has Development Approach, which covers methodology and constraints. Step 4 also omits the Solution Approach confirmation that the table requires (L167). That confirmation is itself a structural question, which L141-142 forbids. Align the two.
